title: Quiz: Diagnostic Plots and Model Comparison

questions.text: In the Residuals vs Fitted plot, you see a U-shaped curve in the residuals (positive at both extremes, negative in the middle). What does this indicate?
options: The mean function is non-linear — a quadratic or log term is needed
There are influential outliers that should be removed
questions.explanation: A U-shape (or any curve) in the Residuals vs Fitted plot indicates that the mean function is mis-specified — the model assumes a linear relationship but the true relationship is curved. Adding a squared term, a log transformation, or a spline would fix this.

questions.text: In the Normal Q-Q plot, if points lie exactly on the 45° diagonal, the residuals follow a perfect normal distribution.
questions.explanation: The Normal Q-Q plot compares the empirical quantiles of the residuals to the theoretical quantiles of a standard normal. If residuals are exactly normal, their quantiles match those of the normal distribution and all points fall on the diagonal line y = x.

questions.text: AIC = 2k − 2log(L̂). Model A has AIC = −3,200. Model B has AIC = −3,180. Which model is preferred?
options: They are equivalent — the difference is less than 2
Neither — AIC cannot compare models with different numbers of parameters
questions.explanation: Lower AIC is better. Model A has AIC = −3,200 which is lower than −3,180. The difference is 20 AIC units — strong evidence (> 10) in favour of Model A. AIC is specifically designed to compare models with different numbers of parameters.

questions.text: anova(mod1, mod2) produces F = 5,473, p-value < 2.2e-16. What is the null hypothesis being tested?
options: That mod1 and mod2 have the same AIC
That all additional coefficients in mod2 (compared to mod1) are simultaneously equal to zero
That the residuals of mod2 are normally distributed
That mod2 has lower RMSE than mod1
questions.explanation: The F-test for nested models tests H₀: all extra parameters in mod2 (beyond those in mod1) are simultaneously zero. Rejecting this null means that at least one of the extra predictors explains a statistically significant amount of variance — mod2 is the better model.

questions.text: In the Residuals vs Leverage plot, a diamond has high leverage but a very small residual. Should you be concerned?
options: Yes — high leverage always means the point is influential
No — influence requires both high leverage AND a large residual. A high-leverage, low-residual point lies on the fitted line and does not distort the estimates
Yes — high-leverage points should always be removed
No — Cook's distance is only relevant for large samples
questions.explanation: Cook's distance = (leverage × residual²) / (variance × parameters). A point with high leverage but near-zero residual has near-zero Cook's distance — it is not influential because it happens to fall close to the fitted line even though it is far from the centre of the predictor space.

questions.text: A non-flat red line in the Scale-Location plot confirms that the residuals have constant variance (homoscedasticity).
questions.explanation: A non-flat line in the Scale-Location plot indicates heteroscedasticity — the variance of residuals changes with fitted values. A flat red line indicates constant variance. The Scale-Location plot is specifically designed to make non-constant variance visible.
